titre: Where monitoring runs, and what stays local.
lede: Transaction monitoring handles the most sensitive table a bank holds. This tool's answer is structural: its public data is written and generated, so not one module is allowed to reach the network, and the two files you measure with never leave your machine.

sections.h2: The network allowlist is empty, and a test traverses each file
html: Routing downloads model weights once; Screening downloads public sanctions lists. Monitoring downloads no file: its sealed public record is built from written cases and seeded variants, so the allowlist of modules that may touch the network is empty, with the comment saying exactly that. A structural test traverses each source file for network sites (fetch, node:http and kin, WebSockets) and fails the suite if any module grows one; the detector first proves it can see a planted call, so its zero means looked and found none.

verif.p: Run the suite. The walk fails if any file gains a network site.

cmd.n: fails if any module touches the network; the allowlist is empty

sections.h2: No real transaction, no real person, anywhere public
html: Each account, amount and date in the sealed public record was written for the typology it illustrates or generated from those cases under a seed. There is no anonymised customer data, because the customer data is simply absent. The file that holds the cases states this in its own header, and each case carries the one-sentence reason it was written.

verif.p: The cases file declares itself, case by case.

cmd.c: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('src/cas-etiquetes.json')); print(d['provenance'], len(d['cas']), 'cases, each with a written reason')"
cmd.n: prints: authored 84 cases, each with a written reason

sections.h2: Your two files stay yours, and the outputs carry no value
html: The measurement runs at your desk: it reads your dispositioned alerts and transactions in memory and writes its outputs next to your files and nowhere else: counts, rates, intervals and verdicts by your alert id. No account id, no amount, no transaction date and no country from your data leave the machine. Your alert ids do survive as verdict keys, so choose them opaque.
There is no callback, no telemetry, no account to create. The whole measurement is a local process reading two CSV files at your desk.

verif.p: Measure a file holding an invented amount and account id, then search the outputs for them.

cmd.c: grep -r "the amount you invented" your-alerts-measured.md your-alerts-measured.json
cmd.n: finds nothing; the outputs carry verdicts and no values

sections.h2: Sealed, offline, and re-measured only out loud
html: The sealed public record is sealed by a content content hash; a hand-edited figure fails loudly, and re-measuring over an existing record requires an explicit flag on the command line, where an auditor can see it. The whole suite runs with the network cut, which for this tool is the only behaviour it has.

verif.p: Cut the network, run everything, then recompute the seal.

cmd.n: says: already sealed, and the seal matches
